candidate_interpretation: Fires on DNA-domain questions about the physical/enzymatic process of nucleic-acid synthesis and polymerase chemistry (primer removal, exonuclease proofreading, translesion synthesis, polymerase mechanics), concentrated in Replication, Mutations_Repair and Transcription_Translation subdomains and largely silent outside DNA.
evidence_supporting: 108/137 discovery and 90/122 confirmation firing tokens are DNA; top examples in both subsets are explicitly about polymerase/primer/exonuclease mechanics (DNA_004945 translesion polymerases, DNA_003461 'DNA polymerase iota... translesion synthesis', DNA_000226 '3'-to-5' exonuclease... corrects nucleotides'). 6 (discovery) / 7 (confirmation) Tier-1 confirmed template families recur across ~19-21 subdomains. All 3 different_domain_same_surface_form counterexamples (SCIENCE prompts using an identical sentence frame about unrelated cell/molecular biology) failed to fire, ruling out a pure surface-template explanation.
evidence_contradicting: Of 5 same_concept_different_template counterexamples (closely related DNA replication/repair questions), only 1 fired (DNA_000149, helicase/synthesis uncoupling); 4 did not fire (photolyase reversal, supercoiling/unwinding, polymerase-template association, unrepaired-lesion persistence), so the concept does not generalize to all DNA-synthesis-adjacent questions. Template diversity is Tier-3-heavy (81/87 discovery, 77/84 confirmation prompts unclustered), so the apparent topical breadth rests mostly on unconfirmed template relationships. A 'large_divergence' flag on script_language_score is reported but both values are near zero (0.09 vs 0.03) and likely not meaningful.
domain_dependence: Treated as a domain-specific candidate (strong_domain_concentration stratum, concentration ~7.0). Concentration in DNA (~80-90% of firing) is expected and not penalized; internal diversity was assessed instead -- spread across Replication, Mutations_Repair, Transcription_Translation, and Structure subdomains with 6-7 confirmed Tier-1 families, which is modest but real diversity rather than a single recurring question.
script_language_dependence: Not a meaningful axis for this feature: script_language_score is near zero in both subsets (0.09/0.03); the reported divergence flag is a ratio artifact of two tiny numbers, not evidence of script sensitivity.
potential_polysemanticity: Possibly bundles two related subthemes: (a) polymerase/primer/exonuclease chemistry proper, and (b) replication-fork/strand-synthesis logistics (leading/lagging strand, Okazaki fragments). Both appear in top examples, and the counterexample failures suggest the feature covers a narrower slice of 'DNA synthesis' than the full topic.

script_language_dependence: Not applicable (script_language_score near zero in both subsets).
